## Analysis

**Best move:** Qh4+

**Main line:** Qh4+ Kg1 Ne2#

**Motif:** Attraction (the check forces the king to g1, where it's mated by the knight check)

**Coaching Note (79 words):**

Your queen and knight can work together to hunt the exposed king. When you play Qh4+, White's king has only one square—g1. That retreat is fatal because your knight on d4 delivers checkmate on e2, controlling both escape squares (f1 and g1). The lesson: always look for loose kings and forcing sequences that exploit them. Check the forcing moves first—checks, captures, threats—rather than defensive moves. A healthy attack beats defense almost every time at club level.
